title: Past, Places, and Opinions
subject: inggris
summary: Simple past, there is/are, comparatives, question words, reading about Banten, and facts versus opinions.
objectives: use the simple past with time words
use there is and there are
compare two things with -er and more
ask questions with what, where, when, and who
tell a fact from an opinion

sections.title: Talking about the past
sections.html:
Time words like yesterday, last week, and ago tell us to use the past form. Regular verbs add -ed (play → played). Some verbs are irregular (go → went, eat → ate, see → saw).

"Yesterday I go to school" is almost right. Look at "yesterday" and change the verb: "Yesterday I went to school."

sections.title: There is, there are
sections.html: There is one tall tower. There are many visitors. Use is with one thing and are with many.

sections.title: Comparing
sections.html:
Comparativeshort words: big → bigger, tall → taller
long words: beautiful → more beautiful

sections.title: Question words
sections.html: What for things, where for places, when for time, who for people. "Where do you live?" "I live in Serang."

sections.title: Fact or opinion?
sections.html: A fact can be checked: "The Great Mosque of Banten is in Banten Lama." An opinion is what someone thinks or feels: "It is the most beautiful mosque in the world." Words like best, most beautiful, and boring often signal opinions.
